brief: Banking app with no monthly fees and early direct deposit. Mainly younger and mid-income Americans, with a goal of account signups. Needs to comply with financial advertising rules.

profile.business_summary: A mobile banking app offering early direct deposit and no monthly fees, targeting younger and mid-income Americans with the goal of driving new account signups under financial advertising compliance.

relevant_tags.why: Younger, mid-income consumers seeking no-fee banking highly value digital convenience.
Digitally native DTC shoppers are comfortable adopting mobile-first financial services.
While free, a banking app represents an ongoing, continuous relationship similar to a digital subscription.

persona_conflicts.conflict: disinterested_in: trendy language, prefers heritage and quality-focused
persona_conflicts.evidence: Banking app with no monthly fees and early direct deposit targeting younger and mid-income Americans.

note_signals.why: Marlowe & Co. targets older, affluent women, which clashes with the advertiser's target of younger, mid-income Americans.
Linden Park has a high-AOV, conservative brand sensibility that does not align with a budget-friendly, younger-skewing banking app.
Velvetline's Gen Z and younger millennial audience directly matches the advertiser's target demographic.

profile.gate_reason: The product, target audience, and key value propositions are clearly defined, allowing for immediate planning on publishers with younger, convenience-oriented demographics.

pricing.rationale: Pay per click (verifiable without trusting a pixel). Market price to win a page view on these hosts: $0.53-$0.72 per click (median $0.61), from the simulated auction against the other campaigns. 'balanced' bidding tries to win up to 60% of each host's page views; the planned bid per host is the price that wins its planned share.
pricing.tcpa_unlock: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded.

allocations.rationale: market price $0.53-$0.72 (median $0.61); bidding $0.37 wins ~0% of page views, paying ~$0.37 per click (second price)

phases.name: learning
phases.rule: planned bid per host; pacing only
phases.why: stable bids so measured rates aren't confounded

phases.name: maximize
phases.rule: planned bid x pacing x conversion likelihood, up to the ceiling

adjustments.reason: Under-delivering vs the daily plan -> bid up a little; over-delivering -> bid down.
Bid higher when the shopper looks like a likely converter (persona match vs the host's average shopper).

bid_strategy.rationale: Maximise conversions within the budget; the ceiling per host is the price that wins your 'balanced' share.
